## Summary Analysis

| Class | Key Features | Match to Test Image |
|---|---|---|
| **Panama Disease** | Intense full-leaf yellowing, brown necrotic streaks, advanced wilt | Moderate — test shows early-stage diffuse midrib yellowing |
| **Yellow/Black Sigatoka** | Discrete dark brown/black spots with yellow halos | No — test has no distinct spots |
| **Bunchy Top** | Stunted, bunched upright leaves, necrotic margins | No — test shows large spreading leaves |
| **Cordana Leaf Spot** | Brown oval spots with orange-yellow halos on green leaf | No — test has no discrete lesions |

**Key features of test image:**
- Large banana leaves with **diffuse yellowing concentrated near the midrib/pseudostem base**
- Yellowing radiates outward from midrib, outer leaf portions remain green
- **No discrete spots, lesions, or necrotic streaks**
- Multiple leaves affected

The pattern of diffuse chlorosis radiating from the midrib/base without discrete lesions is most consistent with **Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt)** at an early stage — the vascular disruption causes systemic yellowing starting near the leaf base/midrib, which progresses to the intense full-leaf yellowing seen in the advanced reference. The complete absence of spots rules out all the foliar spot diseases.
